thread:
matt: Quick question for people who've flown with camera rigs to offsites — is it better to carry everything on or ship the big case?
anya: Carry-on if you can. Batteries and stuff usually can't go in checked.
jess: Yup. Li-ion in carry-on only per TSA. Also saves you from lost baggage nightmares.
sam: Shipping is nice if it's a big pelican case and you don't want to lug it through airports. But customs/insurance is a pain for international.
linda: If you carry, bring a small TSA-approved cable lock and pad the lenses in a separate pouch.
matt: Good recs — does anyone have a lightweight packing foam suggestion?
jess: I use cheap PE foam sheets from Amazon and cut the dividers with an X-acto. Super light and modular.
anya: Also get lens caps on and put silica packets in the case — humidity on East Coast offsites killed a lens for me once.
sam: Pro tip: put the camera body with lens attached in the backpack on the plane, not in the pelican. Easier to access and less risk.
linda: Batteries in a small clear pouch in carry-on for security — they never complain and it's quicker.
matt: Anyone tried shipping via UPS prepaid crate vs checked as oversized? Which is safer?
jess: UPS ground with declared value + signature required is pretty safe. But schedule it to arrive a day early.
anya: If you're checking, take out flash/flares and pack them with you. Also wrap fragile tags around handles.
sam: Also file a quick photo inventory on your phone and email it to yourself. Makes insurance claims so much faster.
travel-bot: Reminder: For international travel, batteries in carry-on only. Check local customs rules for camera gear.
matt: Budget question — does the company reimburse shipping for offsite equipment?
anya: Yes, submit as "equipment transport" under travel expenses and include tracking + receipt. Finance reimbursed mine last offsite.
jess: If you're sharing kit with teammates: label your case with name + cell. People forget.
linda: Also, consider a small foldable shoulder strap for the pelican — saves your back running to taxis.
matt: Poll: carrying main camera on plane or shipping it? :camera_flash:
anya: carrying :thumbsup:
jess: carrying :thumbsup:
sam: shipping :thumbsup:
linda: carrying :thumbsup:
matt: Awesome — sounds like carry-on wins unless it's huge. Thanks team!
jess: Also, if anyone wants to borrow a basic kit for the offsite, I can bring a 24-70 + spare battery. DM me.
anya: Legend.
travel-bot: Note: If flight is red-eye, consider stowing drinking water and a mini dry towel for quick sensor clean if needed (not while on plane obviously).
matt: haha noted. packing list I'll post in #offsite-logistics later.
anya: Please include a short photo checklist. makes setup faster.
matt: Will do — thanks everyone :raised_hands:
